title: Drawback Chess, But YOU Don't Know MY Drawback
summary: Online Drawback Chess (drawback chess website, purple UI) against random human opponents (e.g. 'Jolyne Kujo', 'lazy indigo dolphin'). Each player gets a random secret drawback; it is a king-capture variant (no check/checkmate - you win by capturing the king; illegal-move highlighting forces the drawback). In this episode the narrator flashes his own drawback for two seconds and then deduces it live with the viewers. Game 1 (Black): his drawback was 'Devil on your shoulder' (must obey the devil's suggested worst move at least every 8th move), opponent's 'Religious dispute' (if opponent moves a bishop you must move a bishop) - he wins by capturing the king. Later drawbacks include 'Stop stalling' (pieces can't move laterally), 'Shapeshifter' (queen...), 'Cheerleaders' (non-pawn pieces can only capture when adjacent to one of your pawns). He wins at least one game.
rules: Standard starting position; king-capture rules: no check, a king can be captured and that ends the game; moving into check is allowed.
Each side is assigned one random drawback from a large list; your own drawback may be hidden (this video: shown for 2 s then hidden), opponent's is hidden until the end.

Drawback examples from the video: Devil on your shoulder (a devil suggests the worst move each turn; if you disobey 7 turns in a row you must obey on the 8th); Religious dispute (if opponent moves a bishop, you must move a bishop); Stop stalling (your pieces can't move laterally/sideways); Cheerleaders (your non-pawn pieces can only capture when adjacent to one of your pawns); Shapeshifter (queen-related, details cut); Cowardly (if your opponent captures, you must move backwards); Death wish (if you can move into check you must).
The UI only allows moves legal under your drawback; forced moves are highlighted (e.g. a pawn/square highlighted).
Info board at game end reveals both drawbacks.

current_impl_issues: Legacy 'drawback' uses a tiny home-made list of 14 move restrictions and standard check rules. Real Drawback Chess is king-capture (no check) with named drawbacks such as Devil on your shoulder, Religious dispute, Stop stalling, Cheerleaders, Shapeshifter, Cowardly, Death wish; conditional/forcing drawbacks (must-move rules) are not expressible as simple move filters.
This episode's twist: player's own drawback shown briefly (2 s) then hidden; legacy just hides it.
